name: Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist

fee.note: Published exam-only price; includes two exam attempts, two exam-simulator sessions and 12 months to schedule. Bundles with a course or a subscription cost more.

exam.format: Online, proctored, performance-based exam: 15–20 tasks solved at a command line running Kubernetes (v1.37 at the time of checking), in two hours. A passed CKA is required first.

access.retake: One free retake is included if the first attempt is not passed; it must be taken within the 12 months of eligibility that start at purchase, with no enforced wait beyond scoring (up to 24 hours) and the 24-hour booking lead time.
access.accommodations: Candidates with disabilities send the Test Accommodations Form at least two weeks before the exam, before scheduling it; requests are reviewed case by case.

scope: Securing container-based applications and Kubernetes platforms during build, deployment and runtime: cluster setup and hardening, system hardening, microservice vulnerabilities, supply chain security, and monitoring, logging and runtime security.
requirements: Candidates must have taken and passed the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam before attempting the CKS. The CNCF program page adds that the CKA does not have to be active.
ai_policy: Check the current assessment rules. AI-assisted study does not imply permission during the exam.
caveats: The curriculum PDF linked from the certification page is the older v1.34 file; the CNCF repository's v1.37 curriculum has the same weights.
Earning or recertifying the CKS on or after June 18, 2026 also extends the CKA to the new CKS expiry date (Linux Foundation CARE program).
Exam tasks are shown in English, Japanese or Simplified Chinese, and candidates can switch language during the exam.

prep.title: Linux Foundation: Kubernetes Security Essentials (LFS260)
prep.note: Designed as preparation for the CKS; also sold in a bundle with the exam.

prep.title: Killer.sh CKS simulator
prep.note: Two 36-hour sessions of 17 graded questions are included with the exam registration.

domains_note: Weights from the Linux Foundation certification page, 'Domains & Competencies' section, read 2026-11-17; the CNCF CKS curriculum v1.37 PDF gives the same weights.
